subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu support automatic group-sender agent provisioning, and what authorization, memory, lifecycle, quota, and routing contract should it expose?
rationale: The requested behavior would turn group-chat sender identities into durable agents with workspaces, tools, skills, config, memory, and costs; automation can prove the gap but cannot choose that product and security boundary.

options.title: Design generic identity-to-agent contract first
options.body: Create an opt-in, admin-authorized lifecycle and memory contract that Feishu can implement without Feishu-only hidden policy.

options.title: Keep session-only routing plus explicit subagents
options.body: Continue using group_sender or group_topic_sender session scoping, static bindings, and explicit thread-bound sessions_spawn until a broader contract is approved.

options.title: Defer to deployment-specific plugins
options.body: Leave automatic group-sender provisioning to external deployments unless a missing OpenClaw channel or agent API seam is identified.

recommendation.title: Design generic identity-to-agent contract first
recommendation.body: Create an opt-in, admin-authorized lifecycle and memory contract that Feishu can implement without Feishu-only hidden policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The request starts with Feishu group-chat ownership, and the package metadata identifies m1heng as the Feishu plugin contact before any shared core seam is added.
